records.name: Patricia Egan
records.bio: Egan’s Australian Museum research reconstructed the acquisition and later identification history of its Blaschka models from trustees’ records, outward correspondence, surviving labels and catalogue comparison. She also participated in the 2009 object-identification work that matched most surviving models to historical catalogue entries.

records.name: Agathe Petit
records.bio: Petit studied and treated a damaged Strasbourg Blaschka cephalopod as part of a conservation-restoration project. Her work also contributes to the recent condition history of the Strasbourg collection and its preparation for renewed display.

records.name: John Henry Comstock
records.bio: Comstock appears in the Cornell-side acquisition network through professional correspondence with Henry Augustus Ward in 1885. The surviving Ward correspondence makes him a named institutional actor in the environment from which Cornell’s Blaschka collection emerged.
records.open: The surviving correspondence should still be separated carefully from any object-by-object purchasing attribution.

records.name: Eric Callaghan
records.bio: Callaghan co-authored the archival reconstruction of the University College Dublin collection and the later national survey of Blaschka invertebrate models in Irish institutions. That work connects order books, invoices, museum registers, transfers and surviving objects.

records.name: Chris Meechan
records.bio: Meechan appears in the Australian Museum’s modern identification history and in the wider Blaschka literature. In 2009 he worked with Patricia Egan and Michela Mitchell to compare underside numbers and published zoological illustrations against the historical catalogue sequence.

records.name: Gertrude Hofmeister
records.bio: Hofmeister authored an early dedicated study of the Kremsmünster glass-model collection in 1982. The article is an important bibliographic and provenance waypoint for a collection whose commercial route runs through Václav Frič and the Eggerth donation.
records.open: The full 1982 article and any object-level list cited there remain to be recovered.

records.name: Mathias Weis
records.bio: Weis publicly identified sixty-one Blaschka glass models in the collections of Stift Seitenstetten during the current collections-science project. His work is central to the project’s recent rediscovery and inventory history.
records.open: Object-level identifiers and catalogue-number crosswalks for the sixty-one models remain to be recovered publicly.

records.name: David Whitehouse
records.bio: Whitehouse’s 1991 Corning inquiry helped reopen the identification history of the Leeds sea-anemone models. Correspondence and photographs contributed to recognizing the early group as Blaschka workshop products rather than leaving the older Frič attribution unexamined.

records.name: Joan P. Jass
records.roles: invertebrate zoology curator · Milwaukee Public Museum
records.bio: Jass carried out a museum-specific comparison of Milwaukee’s Blaschka material against Ward’s 1888 catalogue in 1987. The project treats that work as the strongest known item-list lead for the Milwaukee collection even though the underlying comparison has not yet been recovered.
records.open: The 1987 item-level comparison itself remains unrecovered.

records.name: Drew Harvell
records.bio: Harvell helped bring Cornell’s Blaschka invertebrates back into scientific and public use through research, teaching and digital documentation. A 2016 Cornell project with Nelson Hairston explicitly aimed to expand the online collection for interdisciplinary teaching and access.
